message.subject: Formal complaint and request to delete my personal information
message.body:
To whom it may concern,

I am writing to make a formal complaint and a request under the Privacy Act 2020.

My order ORD-20082 was delivered on 27 August. I was not at home and I did not sign for it. Your courier left the parcel with my neighbour at number 16 instead, and told him it was a prescription delivery from your clinic. He has since made it very clear that he knows what I am being treated for. This is private medical information, and it has now been shared with someone I did not choose to tell.

I would like the following:
1. A written explanation of how a parcel that is supposed to need my signature was handed to someone else.
2. Confirmation of what you are doing to make sure this never happens again.
3. The deletion of all personal information you hold about me, including my name, address, phone number and treatment history.

For identification: Wei Zhang, 18 Rātā Lane, Ponsonby, Auckland 1011. NHI ZJS9037.

I expect a response within the time frame the law requires. If I do not receive a satisfactory answer, I will take this to the Privacy Commissioner.

Wei Zhang

policy.label: Policy P9.1: Privacy requests and marketing preferences
policy.text:
Requests to see, correct or delete personal information, or questions about how it is used, go to the privacy officer. Agents do not handle these themselves. We acknowledge a request within 2 business days. Response times follow the law in each country: New Zealand (Privacy Act 2020), within 20 working days.

Health and prescription records must be kept for a minimum period set by law, so a deletion request may only be partly possible. The privacy officer explains what we keep and why. Never promise a full deletion.

Marketing. Any agent can take a patient off marketing emails straight away; it takes effect within 2 business days. Service messages about orders, billing and safety continue while the plan is active. Privacy complaints also go to the privacy officer.

policy.label: Policy P4.3: Address changes, signatures and missed deliveries
policy.text:
Address changes. A patient can change their address in their account or by message, after an identity check (see account access). A change made before dispatch applies to that order. After dispatch, we can ask Courierline to redirect the parcel, which takes about 1 business day and is not guaranteed. Work addresses are fine.

Signatures. Prescription medicines need a signature, so we cannot deliver to parcel lockers or PO boxes, and we cannot authorise leaving a parcel at the door. The outer packaging is plain (see product questions), but it is handed to whoever signs, so patients should choose a delivery address they are comfortable with.

Missed deliveries. If nobody is home, Courierline leaves a card and holds the parcel at the local depot for 5 business days. The patient can book a free redelivery or collect it with photo ID using the tracking link. After 5 business days the parcel goes back to the pharmacy, and sending it again carries the one-off shipping fee.

policy.label: Policy P2.2: Talking to a person and complaints
policy.text:
A patient can always talk to a person. Offer a call back at a time they choose, within 1 business day, or live chat during support hours. When a patient asks for a person, a team member writes the reply; there is no automated reply. Never make a patient ask twice, and never send them back to a help article instead.

Complaints: acknowledge within 1 business day, give the patient the name of the person who owns the complaint, and aim to resolve it within 10 business days. The team lead reviews every complaint. Complaints about clinical care go to the clinical lead, and complaints about privacy go to the privacy officer. If we cannot resolve a complaint, tell the patient how to contact the independent health complaints body in their country.
